value.body: A hatchery technician breeds fish or shrimp and raises the young (seed) until they can be stocked on farms. Work includes caring for broodstock, managing larval tanks and live feed, and keeping strict hygiene. Employers include private hatcheries and government fish seed farms.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.F.Sc (some hatcheries also train diploma holders)

items.label: Where you work
items.value: Shrimp and fish hatcheries, often near the coast or reservoirs

items.label: Registered coastal aquaculture farms
items.source: Coastal Aquaculture Authority data, cited in PRS brief on the CAA (Amendment) Bill, 2023

items.label: Total fish production
items.source: Handbook of Fisheries Statistics, Department of Fisheries (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Join a hatchery as a trainee or assistant; hatchery training during the B.F.Sc helps. Work runs in breeding seasons and can involve night shifts.

value.title: At a glance
items: Hours follow the breeding cycle, so shifts can be long in season.
Experience can lead to hatchery manager roles or your own hatchery.
Biosecurity skills carry over to farm and health roles.

value.title: B.F.Sc enrolment
value.note: Bachelor of Fisheries Science, all years of the course. Pool of graduates, not hatchery jobs.
value.source: AISHE reports 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24 (Ministry of Education), programme-wise enrolment table — B.F.Sc., all modes
